clue.text: Garment protecting me in attack

indicators.note: a garment protecting something is wrapped round it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a coat is a garment
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wears a protective coat when under assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To come at someone is the idiom for to attack or rush at them.

clue.text: Fellow beginning to dive into lake is specially-trained soldier

indicators.note: the man and the letter go into the lake's name, which surrounds them

parts.note: Como is an Italian lake
a fellow is a man

indicators.note: beginning to dive means just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soldier is trained to dive into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier from a unit trained for raids and special operations.

clue.text: Liberal follows fashion, for example

indicators.note: the Liberal's letter follows, coming after the word for fashion

parts.note: mode means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician follows the fashion, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a pattern or example to be copied.

clue.text: A church service

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church holds a service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a church service, but the service is a tennis serve that wins outright.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch.

clue.text: Mine's in poor shape? Famous last words

indicators.note: the word for a mine sits inside the jumbled letters
poor shape suggests the letters of shape are in bad order

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A colliery is said to be in poor shape, followed by a famous last line.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Mine's in poor shape?' look like a separate remark; 'poor' gives EAPHS and 'in' places the pit word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Epitaphs are the words inscribed on tombstones, a person's literal last words in public.

clue.text: Writer, female

parts.note: a poet is a writer
the suffix -ess marks a female form, as in actress

explanation.surface: A bare description of a woman who writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetess is a woman who writes poetry, a female writer.

clue.text: Snooty and sweet-smelling?

explanation.surface: Someone haughty who also smells pleasantly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the hyphenated term literally: a nose full of toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is British slang for snobbish; literally, a nose of toffee would smell sweet.

clue.text: Delivering speech about suffering under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under pressure puts the rest below the pressure letter

parts.note: re means about or concerning
aching means suffering

explanation.surface: Someone gives a talk about their suffering while under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Preaching is delivering a sermon, a kind of speech.

clue.text: Staid and extremely sensible boyfriend?

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: a date can be the person one is going out with

explanation.surface: A boyfriend is described as staid and very sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate is a synonym of staid, meaning calm and dignified.

clue.text: Party with crackers and cakes from America

parts.note: a do is a party
crackers and nuts both mean mad

explanation.surface: A party serves crackers alongside American cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Donuts is the American spelling of doughnuts, ring-shaped cakes.

clue.text: A mere drop polluted variety of coral

indicators.note: polluted letters are spoiled and mixed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even a tiny drop of pollution harms a type of coral.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrepore is a reef-building stony coral.

clue.text: Psychoanalyst runs into hostility

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for hostility

parts.note: a feud is long-running hostility
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst meets hostility from patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis.

clue.text: Could be viewed as A level film?

parts.note: the letters A L L placed around the name Eve spell out A level

explanation.surface: A film might be studied at A level.
explanation.walkthrough: A level is a British school-leaving exam; here the phrase is a letter picture to decode.
explanation.definitionFit: All About Eve is a 1950 film starring Bette Davis.

clue.text: Snubbing bishop, then running away?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rushing off means running away

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a bishop and then hurries away.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing off someone means dismissing them curtly, snubbing them.

clue.text: Boat is here — about time

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A boat arrives at about the right time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is short for catamaran, a twin-hulled boat.

clue.text: Talk about record originally set by America

parts.note: a disc is a record
US is America

indicators.note: originally means the start of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: People discuss a record first released in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means next to: the S of set stands beside US, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss is to talk about a topic.

clue.text: Millwall initially subdued by Preston's organised players

indicators.note: a team subdued by another is held within it, so one letter is enclosed
organised means arranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the name Preston with its s, all used as letters

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Football: Millwall are overpowered early by Preston's well-drilled team.
explanation.walkthrough: Millwall and Preston North End are English football clubs. 'organised' rearranges PRESTONS, and M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmen are players of sports.

clue.text: Bright learner is eclipsed by second one

indicators.note: something eclipsed is covered over, so the learner letter is hidden within the others

parts.note: a unit is one
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A clever student is outshone by the runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlit means lit by the sun, hence bright.

clue.text: Someone choosing gutted eel and freshwater fish

parts.note: a picker is someone who chooses

indicators.note: a gutted word loses its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An angler selects a gutted eel and a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pickerel is a small North American pike, a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Judges found next to this tree?

definitions.text: Judges found next to this tree?

parts.words: Judges found next to this tree?
parts.note: the Bible book of Judges follows a book of the same name as a desert tree, the yucca native to the American Southwest

explanation.surface: Judges are found standing beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Judges are not people here but the Old Testament book; the book before it shares its name with a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Joshua precedes Judges in the Bible, and the Joshua tree is a yucca.

clue.text: A state copper's put in charge

indicators.note: the copper's letters are put in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A policeman from a state is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a charge against someone.

clue.text: One gets on with it, twirling weapon

indicators.note: twirling turns the whole sequence round so it reads backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ages means gets older, gets on
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Someone carries on, twirling a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One gets on' reads like someone mounting a horse; 'twirling' turns the whole run, IAGESSA, back to front, and 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: AA fixes vehicle's motor problem

indicators.note: the two letters fix the vehicle between them, holding it in place

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The AA repairs a car's engine fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British breakdown service. 'motor' means muscular movement, not an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is loss of control of bodily movement, a motor disorder.

clue.text: I'm about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround the other word

parts.note: taken as its letters
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are about to stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for in the same place, used in references.

clue.text: Amount of information (not much)

explanation.surface: A small quantity of data.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a binary digit, the smallest unit of information; a bit also means a small amount.

clue.text: What might lovers do repeatedly, being close?

explanation.surface: Lovers kissing again and again, nestled close together.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is to kiss; doing it repeatedly is necking and necking.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck and neck means level in a race, so close that neither leads.

clue.text: English levy up about a penny for Brit abroad

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the penny letter
in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tax is a levy

explanation.surface: An English tax goes up by about a penny for those living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAX into XAT, which goes round P; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) is someone living outside their native country.

clue.text: Silent love film

parts.note: dumb means silent
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A silent romantic film.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is a 1941 Disney animated film about a flying elephant.

clue.text: Sporty type, one wearing short blue pullover

indicators.note: the one letter wears the clothing around it, so it sits inside
short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: sky blue is a colour, so the sky stands for blue
a jumper is a pullover
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls on a sky-blue sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the blue word; 'wearing' makes the one letter sit inside the clothing, as a wearer is inside a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jumper is an athlete in a winter sport.

clue.text: Woman introduced into tribunal

indicators.note: introduced into means the name sits inside the word

explanation.surface: A woman is brought before a tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: Una is a female given name, so it stands for a woman, a crossword-only shorthand for any name.

clue.text: Engine part having several different forms?

explanation.surface: An engine component that comes in many shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is the pipe system feeding an engine's cylinders; manifold also means many and varied.

clue.text: Finally got stuck in waterway? Hard cheese

indicators.note: something stuck in a canal is placed inside the word

parts.note: a canal is a waterway

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: Getting stuck in a canal is hard luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' looks like the British slang for bad luck; it is a type of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantal is a firm French cheese from the Auvergne.
